bug_report_content:
Title: new multivariate vector optimizers cannot be used with large number of weights
Type: Bug | Priority: Critical | Status: Closed | Resolution: Fixed

Description:
When using the Weigth class to pass a large number of weights to multivariate vector optimizers, an nxn full matrix is created (and copied) when a n elements vector is used. This exhausts memory when n is large.

This happens for example when using curve fitters (even simple curve fitters like polynomial ones for low degree) with large number of points. I encountered this with curve fitting on 41200 points, which created a matrix with 1.7 billion elements.

Comments:

[Luc Maisonobe]: Fixed in subversion repository as of r1426616.

[Gilles Sadowski]: Keeping the matrix concept, by representing uncorrelated observations with a diagonal weight matrix (instead of an array), allows to solve this issue with minimal changes to the code:
# The optimizer's API is untouched.
# The possibility to have correlated observations is kept.

The attached patch contains a minimal "DiagonalMatrix" implementation, needing overview (ant unit tests).

[Gilles Sadowski]: Changes committed in revision 1426758.

The same problem would occur int the deprecated "o.a.c.m.optimization" package. The same changes must be ported there.

[Gilles Sadowski]: bq. The same changes must be ported there.
